newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends firmer after bullish spec report.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends firmer after bullish spec report.

text.p: NYCE cotton ended firmer in heavy trading after the latest speculator/hedge report from the exchange was seen as bullish, traders said.
The spec/hedge report released by NYCE before the market opened, revealed that speculators were 19.6 percent short by close of trade on Friday, up sharply from the previous week.
Traders said the report sparked an early rally which fizzled by midday after light shortcovering by funds dried up.
Another upward push in the afternoon nudged May through the resistance level of 76.00 cents, but the gains were quickly pared for the second time.
May closed 0.74 cent firmer at 75.96 cents per pound, traded 76.40 to 75.35 cents. Volume was heavy at an estimated 16,000 lots, compared to Monday's official 6,456 lots.
At close on Monday open interest was 64,073 lots, down 1,797 from Friday.
Prudential Securities analyst Ernest Simon said the market was largely waiting for the USDA March 31 report on the 1997/98 prospective cotton plantings.
